name: Centro and the Costanera
tagline: The seafront avenue along Golfo Nuevo
description: Puerto Madryn's centre runs parallel to a long seafront where the whales come into the bay between June and December, close enough to watch from the promenade. The shops, restaurants, dive operators and the bus terminal are all within a few blocks, and the town is small enough to cross on foot.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the bay, the dive shops and the restaurants on foot
pros: Whales visible from the shore in season
Dive operators and tour agencies on the front
cons: The highest rents in the town, worse in whale season
The wind comes straight off the water

name: Northern Costanera and Punta Cuevas
tagline: Up the shore past the Ecocentro
description: The coast road running northeast past the Ecocentro museum to Punta Cuevas, where the first Welsh settlers landed in 1865 and dug shelters into the cliff. Housing thins into quieter residential streets with wide bay views, and the beach below is where people swim in summer.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting the bay view and distance from the centre
pros: Ecocentro and the Welsh landing site nearby
Quieter than the centre with the same water
cons: Fifteen to twenty minutes on foot to the shops

name: Residential Madryn
tagline: Inland from the seafront, where the town actually lives
description: The residential grid running back from the coast, with ordinary Argentine houses and low blocks, local shops, schools and the aluminium smelter's workforce. It is unremarkable and it is where rents are lowest, with the seafront a ten-minute walk downhill.
bestFor: Longer stays where the seafront rents are unnecessary
pros: The lowest rents in the town
Ten minutes on foot to the seafront
A year-round community rather than a seasonal one
cons: The smelter is a visible neighbour

name: Puerto Piramides (100 km northeast)
tagline: The only village on Peninsula Valdes
description: The single settlement inside Peninsula Valdes, a hundred kilometres northeast, with a few hundred residents, the whale-watching boats and a beach in a sheltered bay. Everything on the peninsula, the elephant seals, the sea lions and the orcas, is reached from here. Accommodation is limited and books out in season.
bestFor: Whale season stays inside the peninsula rather than in town
pros: The only base inside Peninsula Valdes
Whale-watching boats leave from the beach
Elephant seals and sea lion colonies within the reserve
cons: A hundred kilometres from Puerto Madryn
Very limited accommodation and it books far ahead
Almost no services and weak connectivity

name: Punta Tombo and the Southern Coast (170 km south)
tagline: Half a million penguins on a headland
description: The coast south towards Trelew and Punta Tombo, where one of the largest Magellanic penguin colonies in the world occupies a headland between September and April. Gaiman on the way is a Welsh village with tea houses and chapels, a genuine survival of the 1865 settlement in Chubut.
bestFor: Day trips and short stays around the penguin colony rather than a base
pros: One of the great penguin colonies on earth
Welsh tea houses and chapels at Gaiman
Trelew has the airport and the dinosaur museum
cons: A hundred and seventy kilometres south, so a full day
The colony is seasonal and empty in winter
